svg.title: Exact lattice-state extraction and tensor absorption
svg.desc: Binary words with probabilities proportional to a prescribed lattice state form tuples. The first selected block gives corners of mass tending to one. Summably small discarded masses yield a nonzero infinite corner. Its repeated target copies absorb one more copy by a shift, and type III projection comparison transfers the map to the full factor.

g.text: Exact lattice states inside a binary product
0 < λ < 1 • strictly positive finite densities • countably many target matrix legs
1. Distinct words retain repeated eigenvalue labels
q_j = λ^(k_j) / Z
w_j: k_j initial ones + one 1 in label position j
p(wⱼ) = a qⱼ
First selected block: cₛ = 1 − (1 − a)ˢ
Normalized finite corner = prescribed q-state ⊗ residual matrix state
2. Keep a nonzero infinite corner
cₙ > 1 − εₙ, Σεₙ = 1/4
e = ∧ₙPₙ, φ(e) = ∏ₙcₙ ≥ 3/4
Every target leg is extracted infinitely often.
3. Identify the whole corner
eRλe ≅ Q ⊗ N₁ ⊗ N₂ ⊗ N₃ ⊗ ⋯
All Nₖ carry the same specified product state.
GNS unitary and normal closures: (MIV27.f–i).
4. Shift copies, then transfer the corner isomorphism
New N → position 1; old position k → k + 1; Q stays fixed.
Rλ ⊗ N ≅ eRλe ⊗ N ≅ eRλe ≅ Rλ
Proof: Sections 26–27. The final transfer uses v*v = 1 and vv* = e in the countably decomposable type III factor.
Diagram of exact maps and mass bounds; no scale for matrix dimensions or probabilities.
